To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) HIV Env-APRIl fusion proteins induce high antibody responses to HIV Env, while the responses to APRIL are minimal, (ii) the Env-APRil fusion proteins induce significantly higher antibody responses in rabbits and mice than the unconjugated Env protein and (iii) the Env-CD40 fusion protein induces minimal anti-CD40 responses.

HIV-1 envelope proteins fused to APRIL are more immunogenic than unconjugated HIV-1 envelope, and that the immunogenicity of APRIL is low, in contrast to other cytokine fusion proteins such as IL-21 and IL-15.

HIV-1 envelope gp140 proteins fused to APRIL induced higher antibody responses against gp140 compared to unconjugate Env, but minimal responses against APRIL, and that the antibody responses induced by gp140-CD40L were negligible.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel HIV-1 vaccine candidate, the Env-APRII fusion protein, that is able to induce high titers of neutralizing antibodies against HIV-1.
HIV vaccine development, specifically with the development of HIV envelope (Env)-based vaccines.
the development of novel vaccines against HIV, the virus causing AIDS, and with the development of new strategies for the induction of broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) against HIV.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the fusion of HIV-1 envelope gp140 proteins to APRIL is an effective approach for the induction of high titers of antibodies against the gp140 component, without significant induction of autoantibodies against the APRIL portion.
APRIL is a safe costimulatory molecule that can be used to enhance the immunogenicity of Env-based immunogenic HIV vaccines.
the immunogenicity of the gp140 protein can be enhanced by the APRIL fusion protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fusion of Env-based HIV-1 immunogens to the TNF superfamily member APRIL can enhance Env immunogenicity, and that this approach can be used to design improved HIV-1 vaccines.
APRIL is a very potent B cell activator and costimulatory molecule, but it has minimal potential to induce autoantibodies.
fusion of Env to APRIL enhances Env immunogenicity, but the immunogen is not recognized as foreign and therefore no autoantibodies are induced.
The main takeaway from our work is that
APRIL fusion proteins can be used to improve the immunogenicity of HIV envelope glycoprotein immunogens, while inducing only minimal anti-APRIL responses.
fusion of Env to APRIL or CD40L can enhance Env immunogenicity in mice and rabbits, without inducing significant antibody responses against the costimulatory molecules.
APRIL fusion can enhance the immune responses to Env and that this approach is safe in rabbits and mice, as it does not elicit significant autoantibody responses.
